How to prepare an
ATS-friendly resume PDF.

A resume should be easy to read on screen and easy to extract into an application form. Start with readable text, review the exported file, and add a signature only when the recipient requests one.

By Inklet · Reviewed 8 November 2026

The quick answer

Follow the employer’s file instructions, use ordinary text for your name and experience, and check the saved PDF before submitting. “ATS-friendly” describes an approach to formatting; it does not guarantee a hiring decision or a successful parse in every system.

What does ATS-friendly mean?

An applicant tracking system, or ATS, helps an employer manage applications. Its resume parser may extract details from your file into profile fields. “ATS-friendly resume” means presenting those details in a format that is straightforward to read and extract.

Parsing is only part of an application. A readable PDF cannot establish that you meet a role’s requirements, and a formatting check cannot predict an interview. Review any fields the application fills in from your resume before submitting them.

Choose a readable resume layout

Use a simple reading order, clear section labels such as Experience, Education, and Skills, and consistent formatting. Put essential contact details in the main document text. Greenhouse lists columns, complex tables, graphics, and header or footer contact details among potential parsing problems. These are risks, rather than proof that every such file will fail. Read Greenhouse’s parsing guidance.

When reviewing your layout, imagine someone reading it without the visual styling. Can they tell which job title, employer, dates, and achievements belong together? If that relationship depends on a decorative sidebar or a complicated grid, simplify the source document before exporting it.

Check that your PDF contains readable text

Open the actual PDF you intend to submit, rather than relying on the document editor’s preview. Try selecting a sentence in your experience section. Lever’s documentation suggests highlighting text as a practical check: a file whose text cannot be highlighted may not be parseable. See Lever’s resume parsing explanation.

  1. Select and copy the main resume text.
  2. Paste it into a plain text editor.
  3. Check your name, email, job titles, dates, and bullet points for missing or scrambled content.
  4. If the text is missing or out of order, return to the original document, simplify it, export again, and repeat the check.

This is a useful manual check, not a test against an employer’s ATS. A scanned page or screenshot may need text recognition or a fresh export from its original document. Adding a signature image does not make the rest of a scanned resume readable.

Should you submit a PDF or a Word document?

Use the format requested by the employer or application portal. If it requests a Word document, submit that format. If it accepts PDF, check the exported PDF’s text and layout, and review any application preview or imported fields.

Check the portal’s size limit too. For example, Greenhouse documents a 2.5 MB limit for resume parsing. That is specific to Greenhouse; other platforms can have different limits. Inklet’s 25 MB signing limit is a separate tool limit and does not tell you what a job application accepts. Check the Greenhouse file-size guidance.

AI editing and Harvard-style resume templates

If you use AI to improve your resume, start with your real experience and review every suggested edit. Harvard’s career guidance recommends using AI to help revise existing material, with accurate details and relevant job language in context. Keep claims that you can explain and support. Read Harvard’s advice on AI for resumes.

For a Harvard-style starting point, use the official Harvard College bullet point resume template. It provides editable document options. Replace the example content with your own details and review the exported file. Inklet is an independent PDF tool and is not affiliated with Harvard.

A template name or an AI-generated draft is not an ATS certification. Evaluate the final document you will send, including any edits made after choosing the template.

How to sign your resume PDF when requested

If the recipient requests a visible signature, you can use the free PDF signature tool to add one. Keep your typed name and contact details in the document; the signature is an additional image.

  1. Choose your existing resume PDF in Inklet.
  2. Select Create signature and draw or type your name.
  3. Place the signature in the requested space without covering any text.
  4. Choose Download PDF, open the downloaded copy, and repeat the text and layout checks before sending it.

Inklet adds a visible signature image in your browser. It does not rewrite the resume, run an ATS assessment, or create a certificate-based digital signature. For the complete signing workflow, see how to sign a PDF for free.

Resume PDF checklist before you apply

  • The file matches the employer’s requested format and size limit.
  • The exported text is selectable, and copied text reads in a sensible order.
  • Your name, contact information, work history, and qualifications are accurate.
  • You have checked the actual downloaded copy, including any signature placement.
  • You have reviewed and corrected fields imported into the application.

Keep an editable original for future updates and a separate copy of the file you submitted.

WHEN YOUR RECIPIENT REQUESTS A SIGNATURE

Add your signature to the PDF.

Draw or type it, place it on the page, and download your copy.
